sections.heading: A resource for the whole journey
sections.text: Use the Wasteland Reference Guide to revisit survival principles, understand equipment, plan workshop projects, and find your bearings. The item almanac is one part of this guide.

sections.heading: Find what you need
sections.text: Choose a chapter or search its title and contents. Open the item almanac for discovered item records, or the map for the current schematic preview.

sections.heading: A guide that grows
sections.text: This first edition establishes the chapters and their starting entries. Detailed creatures, locations, combat techniques, and workshop instructions will expand as those systems are designed.

sections.heading: The basis of survival
sections.text: Human survival depends on algae. Settlements maintain algae vats, and personal algae reserves support people traveling in the wasteland. Phagia is the nutritional foundation.

sections.heading: A world without natural water
sections.text: There are no oceans, rivers, rain, or plant life. Liquids extracted from fauna are not automatically drinkable. Industrial usefulness does not establish food safety.

sections.heading: Preparation matters
sections.text: Exposure, distance, depleted resources, and poor planning can compound. Equipment and supplies should be understood before leaving town; exact operating limits belong to the relevant item and gameplay rules.

sections.heading: Read the Broken World
sections.text: The world is shaped by deep canyons, traversable paths, ruins, and ancient structures. Route planning and deliberate movement are central to the journey.

sections.heading: Perpetual twilight
sections.text: The inhabited world lies between the sunward and darkward extremes. Its cycle moves between brighter sunset and deeper twilight. Long shadows contribute to environmental readability.

sections.heading: Map preview
sections.text: The browser map currently shows illustrative Booter, Legger, and camp markers. Its waypoint is a local visual aid; it does not provide live terrain, distance measurements, or movement commands.

sections.heading: Wind, dust, and electricity
sections.text: Windstorms, dense dust storms, and violent electrical storms belong to this world. Weather can affect decisions about routes, shelter, and continuing an outing.

sections.heading: Electrical protection
sections.text: Insulating suits, gloves, and boots exist for electrical handling. Insulation and grounding serve different purposes; neither establishes blanket immunity. Exact protection and storm mechanics remain to be defined.

sections.heading: Equipped and carried
sections.text: Open Inventory to inspect Booter’s equipment and the Legger’s cargo. Possession and equipped status are distinct. The browser equipment picker lets you inspect compatible choices before confirming one.

sections.heading: Body frames and attachments
sections.text: Booter needs an equipped body frame to equip attachments. The Utility harness provides two attachment mounts. The frame controls attachment eligibility; carrying an attachment does not mount it.

sections.heading: A physical companion
sections.text: The Legger is a physically present companion and finite cargo carrier. He has a true world position and must traverse the world to regroup. Cargo does not become remote storage. Mounting and the tradeoff between rider space and cargo belong to the separate expedition proposal.

sections.heading: Understand a finished item
sections.text: Open Workshops and its Crafting tree service to explore a finished item’s requirements. Complex branches are intentional. Track materials you want to find and inspect parts along the way.

sections.heading: Tools and materials
sections.text: Supplied tools can end an input branch. Manufactured crafting components need their own material inputs; gathered, mined, and harvested base resources can end branches. An item’s tier or rarity does not remove its manufacturing requirements.

sections.heading: Plan and make
sections.text: Workstations retain their existing browser sample operations. Tracked items and tracked projects help organize gathering. A visible tree is a design record, not proof that every recipe is executable.

sections.heading: A vulnerable survivor
sections.text: Booter is a trained desert survivor and scrapper. Movement and combat call for commitment and positioning rather than effortless power.

sections.heading: Great hunts
sections.text: Hunts are systemic encounters embedded in the world. Targets may include ancient war machines and massive insectoid organisms. Scouting, preparation, environmental positioning, and risk evaluation matter.

sections.heading: Field records to come
sections.text: Creature-specific behaviors, weaknesses, combat instructions, and encounter records need their own authored entries. This chapter does not assign unapproved enemy statistics or tactics.

sections.heading: An alternative design
sections.text: These expedition rules are a proposal being explored by the browser menu. They remain separate from the existing open-world direction.

sections.heading: Prepare, explore, return
sections.text: Prepare equipment and goods in town, then enter at a random root beacon on persistent terrain. Other run content is procedurally populated. Return to that beacon and complete the departure task to end the run.

sections.heading: Distance creates pressure
sections.text: There is no run timer or danger escalation simply because time passes. The proposal increases danger as the player ventures farther from the beacon. Its exact proximity rules remain open.

sections.heading: Use your haul in town
sections.text: Early runs require returning to town to craft and store goods. Field storage and crafting are later concepts. Begin run remains a browser placeholder.

sections.heading: Find your way around
sections.text: Bumpers switch primary tabs; triggers switch available sub-tabs. Use the D-pad or left stick to navigate and the south face button to select. The right stick scrolls where available.

sections.heading: Inventory and Start
sections.text: Select / View opens Inventory. Start / Menu opens the Start page. The bottom prompts also work as clickable controls. On a keyboard, I opens Inventory and F1 opens Start.

sections.heading: Back one step
sections.text: The east face button or Escape backs out. Close an item picker first. Resource pages return to Start, and Start returns to the page you opened it from. Ordinary town pages return to Play.
